sources.title: Government of Odisha · Literature
sources.note: Ganeswar Mishra, Government of Odisha literary overview: Sarala Das’s fifteenth-century Mahabharata.
sources.inspection: Official overview retrieved in full by Disha during the 20 October review. Only the Sarala period and literary context are used; unrelated date inconsistencies and older present-tense descriptions are not adopted.

sources.title: B. N. Patnaik · Aadi Kavi Sarala and His Mahabharata
sources.note: B. N. Patnaik, Aadi Kavi Sarala and His Mahabharata, 7 November 2019: the poet’s self-presentation and Sakuni’s responsibility for the war’s dead. These readings follow Patnaik’s account.
sources.inspection: Author-published essay directly inspected by Disha and Anvesha, including opening paragraphs, “In Sarala’s retelling” and “Knowing that only Duryodhana.” The selected episodes have not been independently collated against an Odia edition; no complete epic or Sanskrit comparison is claimed. Goddess-inspired authorship is treated as religious self-presentation, not a verified miraculous event.

sources.title: Ujaan Ghosh · Struggling with Kṛṣṇa: Alternative Imaginations in an Odia Mahābhārata
sources.note: Ujaan Ghosh, Struggling with Kṛṣṇa (published 2025; journal volume 2026): biography, “The Disrobing of Draupadī” and note 4. The episode follows his reading of Mohanty, vol. 6, pp. 501–509.
sources.inspection: Open-access HTML inspected by Disha and Anvesha: published 20 August 2025, International Journal of Hindu Studies 30 (2026), 1–23. Ghosh uses Artaballabh Mohanty’s 1965–1968 edition and explains its variant readings and page-based citations in note 4. Draupadi passage discussed at vol. 6 pp. 501–509, especially 502–503. Our account paraphrases Ghosh’s interpretation; no underlying epic facsimile/manuscript collation or full Sanskrit comparison. Article CC BY 4.0; no translated verse reproduced.
